Aspirin resistance: mechanisms and clinical implications. Acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) has been shown to irreversibly interfere with platelet function, an effect that is associated with a reduction in morbid and mortal arterial thrombotic events in multiple clinical studies. This clinical benefit appears to be attenuated by resistance to the antiplatelet effects of aspirin in up to 35% of patients.
